reason: Almost all the weight is on bills that make it easier to end a marriage. Some cap how long rabbinical court divorce cases can take (rows 1, 4). Some let the court rule in severe violence cases (3, 22). Some penalise husbands who refuse to grant a religious divorce: credit card limits, forcing the divorce, automatic divorce, taking away rights (5, 8, 11, 13, 14, 17, 18, 20, 21, 23, 25). Others add prenuptial or mutual respect agreements (6, 9). The rest open a civil route to divorce (2, 7, 10, 12, 16, 19, 24). All are labelled toward agreeing. The price clause 'even if one of the spouses objects' matches the core case: refusing to grant a religious divorce is exactly a spouse objecting. The civil marriage bills (2, 7, 10, 12) also cover civil marriage, but their divorce part fits the statement, and they are still about access to divorce. No change needed.
